title: Perimeter of compound shapes
canonical_examples_source: Arithmetic self-verified; method ref: NCERT Class 5/6 Maths; format ref: bank uk-ks2-2024 maths.

blocks.content: A compound shape, like an L-shape, is made of simpler shapes joined together. Its perimeter is still just the distance all the way around the outside. Quick words: compound shape means a shape made by joining two or more simple shapes together. perimeter means the total distance around the outside edge of a shape.
The perimeter of any shape is the sum of all its outside edges — add every side once.

steps: A shape has outside sides of 3, 4, 3 and 4 cm.

blocks.prompt: A shape has outside sides 3, 4, 3, 4 cm. Perimeter = 3 + 4 + 3 + 4 = ___
blocks.rule: The perimeter of any shape is the sum of all its outside edges.

blocks.content: For an L-shape, work carefully all the way around, adding each edge once, even the extra corners.

blocks.question: To find the perimeter of a compound shape, you:
blocks.explain: Perimeter is always the total of all the outside edges added together.
blocks.rule: Add every outside edge once, going all the way around the shape.

blocks.question: You cut a small 2 by 2 square notch out of one corner of a 6 by 4 rectangle. What happens to the perimeter?
options: It stays 20 — the two new inside edges replace the two edges that were removed
blocks.explain: The original perimeter is 6 + 4 + 6 + 4 = 20. Cutting the corner removes 2 + 2 from the outer edges but adds 2 + 2 as the new notch edges. The amounts cancel, so the perimeter is still 20 — even though the area got smaller.
blocks.rule: Perimeter is the distance around the outside; count every outer edge, including notches.
blocks.principle: Area and perimeter change independently — one can stay the same while the other changes.
canonical_solution: Corner cut removes 2 + 2 of outer edge
But adds 2 + 2 of new notch edge

rubric.look_for: compares edges removed and edges added
sees they cancel, so perimeter is unchanged (20)
notes area can change while perimeter does not

misconceptions.coach: The notch adds new edges equal to those removed, so the perimeter holds.
Area does drop by 4; but perimeter counts the outer path.

blocks.content: No matter how bumpy the shape, the perimeter is every outside edge added up once. Go all the way around. Let's practise!
